hints: Look closely at the pale, elongated cell labelled X and compare it to the darker cell next to it on the right. Which one has a nucleus and dense cytoplasm, and which one looks almost empty?

Remember the phloem partnership: one cell is living but has lost its nucleus to make room for flow, while its neighbour keeps a dense nucleus to control it. Also look at the bottom of X for a perforated end wall.
walkthrough:
**Observe what X looks like**

Look at cell X in the centre. It is long, pale and mostly empty, with only a thin layer of cytoplasm at the edges and no nucleus visible.

Right next to it is a much darker cell with dense cytoplasm and a large dark nucleus. That contrast is a big clue.

**Apply the phloem structure rule**

A mature phloem sieve tube element is alive but highly specialised. It loses its nucleus and most organelles to allow easy mass flow of sucrose, so it looks empty in an electron micrograph.

It is always found beside a small companion cell, which is dense with cytoplasm, mitochondria and a nucleus to provide ATP and control for the sieve element. You can also see a sieve plate with pores at the lower end of X.

**Rule out the other tissues**

This cannot be xylem, because xylem vessel elements are dead, hollow and have thick lignified walls, not a thin peripheral cytoplasm. It cannot be Casparian strip, which is a waterproof band in root endodermis, not a whole cell in the stem.

The pale, enucleate cell with a sieve plate beside a dense companion cell is the classic phloem sieve tube element.

options.A: The companion cell is the small, dark, dense cell to the right of X with a nucleus, not the pale empty cell X itself.
options.B: The Casparian strip is a band of suberin in the endodermis of roots, not a long transport cell in a stem longitudinal section.
options.C: X is pale, elongated, lacks a nucleus, has only peripheral cytoplasm and shows a sieve plate, all classic features of a phloem sieve tube element.
options.D: A xylem vessel element would be dead and empty with a thick lignified wall and no cytoplasm, not a living sieve element with peripheral cytoplasm.
